Highest values

Share of each group's population exposed, by hazard

Population-weighted: total people exposed in the group divided by its total population. Click a hazard to select it, or a group to open its profile.

The black tick is the world value.

Share of the world's exposed people compared with share of world population

Relative exposure index: above 1 means the group carries more than its population share of this exposure.

Bars are coloured by hazard category. The black tick is the world value. Click a bar to select that hazard.

Inside each country, demographic groups are exposed at almost exactly the same rate as the total population (ratios of 0.99 to 1.01). This suggests the age and sex layers were built by applying age shares to the total population grid. Differences between groups in aggregates come mainly from differences between countries. Please check this with the data producer.

The black tick is the world value for the same group.

Number of people in each group exposed to the selected hazard.

% of each demographic group exposed, for every hazard. Click a hazard to select it.

The Degurba sheet splits exposed people into urban centres, urban clusters and rural areas. It gives no total population per settlement class, so it shows where exposed people live, not exposure rates.

Share of exposed people by degree of urbanisation (GHS-DUG Level 1).

Hazards sorted from the most rural to the most urban. Click a hazard to select it.

SSP projections cover the total population only. Hazard footprints are held at 2025, so changes come from population growth and redistribution only. SSP1 and SSP5 have nearly the same population, as do SSP3 and SSP4, so their lines overlap (dashed lines show SSP4 and SSP5).
